name: Ukadpendi
steps: Dry-roast whole wheat flour over low heat for 7–9 minutes, stirring continuously, until nutty and lightly golden. Spread it on a plate so it stops cooking; do not leave raw-flour patches.
Heat oil in a broad pan, splutter mustard and cumin, then cook finely chopped onion and green chilli until the onion softens. Stir in turmeric and salt.
Bring measured water to a boil in the pan. Lower the heat and sprinkle in the roasted flour gradually while stirring firmly to prevent lumps.
Cover and steam over low heat for 5–7 minutes, stirring once, until the flour is cooked and forms moist small crumbs rather than dry powder or a sticky paste.
Fluff with a fork, add lemon juice and coriander, and divide into four bowls. Serve warm while the crumbly texture is distinct.
tips: Roast the flour thoroughly before adding water; raw flour cannot be fixed after steaming.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
